body.en: From the specialized-tables subtopic: `AS NODE` tables hold entities, `AS EDGE` tables hold relationships with implicit `$node_id`, `$edge_id`, `$from_id`, `$to_id` columns. This subtopic covers QUERYING graphs with MATCH, plus T-SQL error handling — both named in the official 'write advanced T-SQL code' skill.

MATCH goes in the WHERE clause of a SELECT whose FROM lists node and edge tables (old-style comma joins). The pattern uses ASCII arrows: `MATCH(Person1-(Follows)->Person2)` — Person1 follows Person2; the arrow points FROM source TO target. Reverse with `<-`: `MATCH(Person1<-(Follows)-Person2)`. Chain hops: `MATCH(a-(f1)->b-(f2)->c)` finds friends-of-friends. Combine multiple patterns with AND (not OR — OR between MATCH predicates is not supported).

sections.code:
-- Who does Alice follow?
SELECT p2.Name
FROM dbo.Person AS p1, dbo.Follows AS f, dbo.Person AS p2
WHERE MATCH(p1-(f)->p2)
  AND p1.Name = 'Alice';

-- Friends of friends (2 hops), excluding direct friends and self
SELECT DISTINCT p3.Name
FROM Person p1, Follows f1, Person p2, Follows f2, Person p3
WHERE MATCH(p1-(f1)->p2-(f2)->p3)
  AND p1.Name = 'Alice' AND p3.Name <> 'Alice';

body.en: `SHORTEST_PATH` (inside MATCH) finds paths of arbitrary length: `MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(p1(-(f)->p2)+))` with `+` = one-or-more hops or `{1,5}` = bounded hops. It requires `FOR PATH` aliases on the repeated tables and graph aggregate functions — `STRING_AGG(...) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH)`, `LAST_VALUE(...) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH)`, `COUNT(...) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH)` — to project values along the path. It returns A shortest path (ties broken arbitrarily), not all of them, and cannot be combined freely with every construct (e.g. no OUTER APPLY around it).

sections.code:
SELECT p1.Name,
       STRING_AGG(p2.Name, '->') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Chain,
       COUNT(p2.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops
FROM dbo.Person AS p1,
     dbo.Follows FOR PATH AS f,
     dbo.Person FOR PATH AS p2
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(p1(-(f)->p2)+))
  AND p1.Name = 'Alice';

body.en: Wrap risky code in `BEGIN TRY … END TRY BEGIN CATCH … END CATCH`. When a (catchable) error occurs in TRY, control jumps to CATCH, where the ERROR_* functions describe it: `ERROR_NUMBER()`, `ERROR_MESSAGE()`, `ERROR_SEVERITY()`, `ERROR_STATE()`, `ERROR_LINE()`, `ERROR_PROCEDURE()`. They keep their values anywhere in the CATCH (unlike @@ERROR, which resets after every statement). Not everything is catchable: compile errors in the same scope, severity ≥ 20 (connection-killing), and attentions (client timeouts) bypass CATCH.

- `THROW` (no args): only inside CATCH, re-raises the original error exactly — the modern default.
- `THROW 50001, 'message', 1;` raises a custom error (error number ≥ 50000, severity always 16, statement must be preceded by a semicolon, message cannot use printf-style formatting).
- `RAISERROR('fmt %s', 16, 1, @arg)`: printf formatting, chooseable severity, `WITH LOG`/`NOWAIT` options, can use sys.messages ids — but doesn't re-raise originals and is discouraged for new code.
Transactions and errors: by default some errors abort only the statement, leaving the transaction open — `SET XACT_ABORT ON` makes errors doom the whole transaction, and in CATCH `XACT_STATE()` tells you: 1 committable, 0 none, -1 doomed (ROLLBACK only).

sections.code:
;THROW 50001, 'Customer not found.', 1;

RAISERROR('Processing step %s failed for id %d.', 16, 1, 'validate', @id) WITH NOWAIT;

body.en: The production template: `SET NOCOUNT ON; SET XACT_ABORT ON;` then TRY with explicit transaction, CATCH with `IF XACT_STATE() <> 0 ROLLBACK; THROW;`. Log-and-rethrow preserves diagnostics while alerting callers. Avoid: empty CATCH blocks (swallowing), PRINT-as-handling, relying on @@ERROR across statements, RAISERROR severities ≥ 19 without WITH LOG (error), and forgetting that THROW statements need the preceding statement terminated with `;`.

examTips.en: MATCH lives in WHERE; FROM uses comma-separated node/edge tables; arrow points from source to target.
Multiple MATCH patterns combine with AND only — OR is not supported.
SHORTEST_PATH needs FOR PATH table aliases and WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) aggregates; + = 1..n hops, {1,n} = bounded.
ERROR_* functions persist throughout CATCH; @@ERROR resets after each statement.
Parameterless THROW only in CATCH; custom THROW needs number ≥ 50000, fixed severity 16, and a preceding semicolon.
CATCH can't catch: same-scope compile errors, severity ≥ 20, client timeouts (attention events).
XACT_STATE(): 1 = commit allowed, -1 = doomed (rollback only), 0 = no transaction.
